rules.title: Every game piece has an owner.
rules.text: 1.7. Every game piece has an owner. Every game piece in play also has a controller.

rules.title: You “own” the pieces you bring to the game (your deck, side deck, Gig dice, etc.).
rules.text: 1.7.1. You “own” the pieces you bring to the game (your deck, side deck, Gig dice, etc.). You’re the “owner” of these pieces.

rules.text: 1.7.2. You “control” the pieces currently in your friendly Gig area, field, Legends area, and Eddies area. You’re the “controller” of these pieces, even if you’re not the owner.

rules.title: Pieces you control are considered “friendly” pieces.
rules.text: 1.7.2.1. Pieces you control are considered “friendly” pieces.

rules.title: Pieces your Rival controls are considered “rival” pieces.
rules.text: 1.7.2.2. Pieces your Rival controls are considered “rival” pieces.

rules.text: 1.7.3. Game pieces can change controllers, but can never change owners.

rules.text: 1.7.3.1. When you take control of a Rival’s game piece, follow the rules in Respect Your Rival.

rules.title: At the end of the game, return all game pieces to their respective owners.
rules.text: 1.7.3.2. At the end of the game, return all game pieces to their respective owners.

rules.title: A game value can be a negative number.
rules.text: 2.10. A game value can be a negative number.

rules.title: When a game value is a negative number, it is treated as 0 for all references and comparisons of values.
rules.text:
2.10.1. When a game value is a negative number, it is treated as 0 for all references and comparisons of values.

> **EXAMPLE:** A Unit has 2 power. An effect reduces its power by 3. The Unit has -1 power, but is treated as having 0 power when attacking, fighting, or when a card effect references its power. If it then gains +2 power, that Unit has 1 power. The order of these effects being applied does not alter this outcome.

rules.title: A value of null ( - ) is not treated as a number.
rules.text: 2.10.2. A value of null ( - ) is not treated as a number. It does not count as 0, and it is not even or odd.

rules.text: 4.10.1. By default, a Gear can be equipped to a friendly Unit or friendly face-up Legend.

rules.text: 4.11. Gears have two textboxes, referred to as the “top textbox” and “bottom textbox.”

rules.title: The top textbox contains effects for the Gear.
rules.text: 4.11.1. The top textbox contains effects for the Gear. These effects are relevant when you play the Gear, and generally not relevant after a Gear is equipped.

rules.title: Effects described in the top textbox apply to the Gear itself, and are not inherited by the Unit or Legend it’s equip…
rules.text:
4.11.2. Effects described in the top textbox apply to the Gear itself, and are not inherited by the Unit or Legend it’s equipped to.

> **EXAMPLE:** A Gear’s top text box contains the reminder text “*(Equip to a friendly Unit or face-up Legend.)*” You equip this Gear to a friendly Unit. That Gear cannot be equipped to another friendly Unit, nor face-up Legend.

rules.title: The bottom textbox contains effects inherited by the Unit or Legend the Gear is equipped to.
rules.text: 4.11.3. The bottom textbox contains effects inherited by the Unit or Legend the Gear is equipped to. Read the bottom textbox as if it's printed on that Unit or Legend.

rules.title: Effects described in a Gear card’s bottom textbox apply only to the Unit or Legend the Gear is equipped to, not the G…
rules.text: 4.11.3.1. Effects described in a Gear card’s bottom textbox apply only to the Unit or Legend the Gear is equipped to, not the Gear itself.

rules.title: A Unit or Legend does not inherit Tags or other characteristics from a Gear equipped to it.
rules.text: 4.11.3.2. A Unit or Legend does not inherit Tags or other characteristics from a Gear equipped to it.

rules.title: When a Legend or Unit moves to a different area (field, trash, hand, etc.), all of its equipped Gear moves with it.
rules.text: 4.12. When a Legend or Unit moves to a different area (field, trash, hand, etc.), all of its equipped Gear moves with it.

rules.title: When a Gear moves with a Unit or Legend to an area outside of the field or Legends area, the Gear isn’t equipped to t…
rules.text:
4.12.1. When a Gear moves with a Unit or Legend to an area outside of the field or Legends area, the Gear isn’t equipped to the Unit or Legend in that area.

> **EXAMPLE:** An equipped Unit has the effect “At the end of your turn, return this Unit to its owner's hand.” When you move the Unit to your hand, you also move its equipped Gear to your hand. Once the cards are in your hand, the Gear is no longer equipped to the Unit. So, if you play the Unit from your hand next turn, the Gear does not move with it.

rules.title: If an equipped Legend moves to an area outside of the Field or Legends area, the Gear follows the Legend to the new a…
rules.text: 4.12.2. If an equipped Legend moves to an area outside of the Field or Legends area, the Gear follows the Legend to the new area. The Gear is no longer equipped in the new area, so it stays there when you remove the Legend from play.

rules.text: 4.12.3. When you bottom-deck an equipped Unit, place the cards at the bottom of your deck in a random order. Randomize them amongst any other cards bottom-decked at the same time. See Bottom-deck.

rules.title: Activate an Effect
rules.text:
8.14. ### Activate an Effect

As an action during your Main phase, you may activate any activated effects on friendly Units or Legends. They may be used during the open state of the main phase. For the full rules on activating effects, see EFFECTS > Activated Effects.

rules.title: You cannot activate [Spend Icon] effects on Lagging Units.

rules.title: If a reaction triggers one or more effects, those effects become pending.
rules.text: 9.11. If a reaction triggers one or more effects, those effects become pending. Both players must resolve all pending effects before the defending player may take another reaction. See EFFECTS > Triggered Effects.

rules.title: At any point during the React Step, while not taking a reaction and while there are no effects pending resolution, th…
rules.text: 9.12. At any point during the React Step, while not taking a reaction and while there are no effects pending resolution, the defending player may choose to end the React Step.

rules.title: If at any point the attacker or the defending Unit is no longer in the field area, the attack ends.
rules.text: 9.13. If at any point the attacker or the defending Unit is no longer in the field area, the attack ends. See ATTACK, FIGHT, AND STEAL > Ending an Attack.

rules.title: When the React Step ends, the attack continues.
rules.text: 9.14. When the React Step ends, the attack continues. If the attack target is a Unit, proceed to the Fight Step. If the attack target is a Gig area, proceed to the Steal Step.

rules.title: The Fight Step only happens if the attack target is a Unit.
rules.text: 9.15. The Fight Step only happens if the attack target is a Unit. If the attack target is a Gig Area, the Steal Step happens instead.

rules.title: During the “Fight Step” of an attack, the attacking Unit and the defending Unit fight.
rules.text: 9.16. During the “Fight Step” of an attack, the attacking Unit and the defending Unit fight.

rules.title: At the start of the Fight Step, apply effects that last “while fighting” and variations thereof.
rules.text: 9.16.1. At the start of the Fight Step, apply effects that last “while fighting” and variations thereof.

rules.title: A “fight” is a game process in which two opposing Units compare power to determine at least one loser and potentially…
rules.text: 9.17. A “fight” is a game process in which two opposing Units compare power to determine at least one loser and potentially one winner.

rules.title: A Unit wins a fight when it has a higher power than the opposing Unit.
rules.text: 9.17.1. A Unit wins a fight when it has a higher power than the opposing Unit.

rules.title: When a Unit wins a fight, the opposing Unit always loses, regardless of power.
rules.text: 9.17.1.1. When a Unit wins a fight, the opposing Unit always loses, regardless of power.

rules.title: A Unit loses a fight when it has equal or lower power than the opposing Unit.
rules.text: 9.17.2. A Unit loses a fight when it has equal or lower power than the opposing Unit.

rules.title: If both Units in a fight have the same power, neither Unit wins and both Units lose the fight.
rules.text: 9.17.3. If both Units in a fight have the same power, neither Unit wins and both Units lose the fight.

rules.title: If a card effect says that a Unit wins or loses a fight, it supersedes any win or loss status determined by power com…
rules.text: 9.17.4. If a card effect says that a Unit wins or loses a fight, it supersedes any win or loss status determined by power comparison.

rules.title: When you determine the loser(s), any effects triggered by the fight (i.e.
rules.text: 9.18. When you determine the loser(s), any effects triggered by the fight (i.e. “when this Unit fights,” “when this Unit loses a fight,” etc.) become pending. Both players must resolve all pending effects before they may defeat the loser(s).

rules.title: After resolving all effects triggered by the fight, resolve the fight’s result.
rules.text: 9.19. After resolving all effects triggered by the fight, resolve the fight’s result.

rules.title: When a Unit loses a fight, the opposing Unit defeats it as a result.
rules.text: 9.19.1. When a Unit loses a fight, the opposing Unit defeats it as a result.

rules.title: When a Unit is defeated, its owner moves it to their trash.
rules.text: 9.19.1.1. When a Unit is defeated, its owner moves it to their trash.

rules.title: A Unit with 0 power cannot defeat a Unit as the result of a fight.
rules.text: 9.19.2. A Unit with 0 power cannot defeat a Unit as the result of a fight.

rules.title: If an effect prevents a Unit from being defeated in a fight, it is still a loser that has lost the fight, it only ign…
rules.text: 9.19.3. If an effect prevents a Unit from being defeated in a fight, it is still a loser that has lost the fight, it only ignores the resulting defeat.

rules.title: After resolving all effects triggered by the fight’s result, the Fight Step and the attack ends.
rules.text: 9.20. After resolving all effects triggered by the fight’s result, the Fight Step and the attack ends. See ATTACK, FIGHT, AND STEAL > Ending an Attack.

rules.title: The Steal Step only happens if the attack target is a Gig area.
rules.text: 9.21. The Steal Step only happens if the attack target is a Gig area. If the attack target is a Unit, the Fight Step happens instead.

rules.title: If the attacked Gig area has no Gigs in it when the Steal Step begins, no Gigs can be or are stolen.
rules.text: 9.22. If the attacked Gig area has no Gigs in it when the Steal Step begins, no Gigs can be or are stolen.

rules.title: During the “Steal Step” of an attack, the attacker attempts to steal one or more Gig dice from the defending Gig area.
rules.text: 9.23. During the “Steal Step” of an attack, the attacker attempts to steal one or more Gig dice from the defending Gig area.

rules.title: At the start of the Steal Step, before choosing which Gigs are stolen, apply effects that last “while stealing” and v…
rules.text: 9.23.1. At the start of the Steal Step, before choosing which Gigs are stolen, apply effects that last “while stealing” and variations thereof. Apply any other effects that modify, prevent, or restrict the attacker’s power or ability to steal.

rules.title: The number of Gigs an attacker steals is based on its power.
rules.text: 9.23.2. The number of Gigs an attacker steals is based on its power.

rules.title: If the attacking Unit has 0 power, it steals 0 Gigs.
rules.text: 9.23.2.1. If the attacking Unit has 0 power, it steals 0 Gigs.

rules.title: If the attacking Unit has 1 or more power, it steals X Gigs (rounded down) according to this formula, where P = the a…
rules.text:
9.23.2.2. If the attacking Unit has 1 or more power, it steals X Gigs (rounded down) according to this formula, where P = the attacking Unit’s power.

`X = (P / 10) + 1)`

> **EXAMPLE:** A Unit with 1 to 9 power steals 1 Gig. A Unit with 10 to 19 power steals 2 Gigs. Continue this pattern for higher power values.

rules.title: The attacking player chooses which Gigs the attacker will steal from the attacked Gig area.
rules.text: 9.23.3. The attacking player chooses which Gigs the attacker will steal from the attacked Gig area.

rules.title: An attacking player may choose to steal any Gig in the defending Gig area, regardless of its value.
rules.text: 9.23.3.1. An attacking player may choose to steal any Gig in the defending Gig area, regardless of its value.

rules.title: If the attacker will steal multiple Gigs, the attacking player chooses the Gigs one at a time.
rules.text: 9.23.3.2. If the attacker will steal multiple Gigs, the attacking player chooses the Gigs one at a time.

rules.title: If the attacker steals more Gigs than are in the attacked Gig area, choose as many Gigs as possible to steal.
rules.text: 9.23.3.3. If the attacker steals more Gigs than are in the attacked Gig area, choose as many Gigs as possible to steal.

rules.title: After all Gigs are chosen, apply any effects that prevent or restrict one or more of those Gigs from being stolen.
rules.text: 9.23.4. After all Gigs are chosen, apply any effects that prevent or restrict one or more of those Gigs from being stolen.

rules.title: After all Gigs are chosen and prevention effects are applied, the attacker steals the Gig(s).
rules.text: 9.23.5. After all Gigs are chosen and prevention effects are applied, the attacker steals the Gig(s).

rules.title: To steal the Gig(s), move all chosen Gigs from the defending Gig area to the attacking Gig area at the same time.
rules.text: 9.23.5.1. To steal the Gig(s), move all chosen Gigs from the defending Gig area to the attacking Gig area at the same time.

rules.title: Multiple Gigs are stolen at the same time, each stolen Gig is considered a separate stolen Gig.
rules.text: 9.23.5.2. Multiple Gigs are stolen at the same time, each stolen Gig is considered a separate stolen Gig.

rules.title: Effects that trigger when a Gig is stolen become pending after a stolen Gig is moved.
rules.text: 9.23.6. Effects that trigger when a Gig is stolen become pending after a stolen Gig is moved.

rules.title: Resolve all pending effects.
rules.text: 9.24. Resolve all pending effects. See EFFECTS > Pending Resolution.

rules.title: After all pending effects from the Steal Step are resolved, the attack ends.
rules.text: 9.25. After all pending effects from the Steal Step are resolved, the attack ends. See Ending an Attack.

rules.title: An attack ends if any of the following are true:
rules.text: 9.26. An attack ends if any of the following are true:

rules.title: The attacking Unit is no longer in the field area.
rules.text: 9.26.1. The attacking Unit is no longer in the field area.

rules.title: The attack target is no longer in the area it was attacked in.
rules.text: 9.26.2. The attack target is no longer in the area it was attacked in.

rules.title: The attack target is no longer a legal attack target for the attacking Unit.
rules.text: 9.26.3. The attack target is no longer a legal attack target for the attacking Unit.

rules.title: An effect has ended the attack.
rules.text: 9.26.4. An effect has ended the attack.

rules.title: An attack can end before reaching the React Step, Fight Step or Steal Step.
rules.text: 9.27. An attack can end before reaching the React Step, Fight Step or Steal Step.

rules.title: If an attack ends before reaching the React Step, Fight Step or Steal Step, no fight happens and no Gigs are stolen.
rules.text: 9.27.1. If an attack ends before reaching the React Step, Fight Step or Steal Step, no fight happens and no Gigs are stolen.

rules.title: If an attack ends while an effect or pending effect is resolving, finish resolving that effect or pending effect.
rules.text: 9.27.2. If an attack ends while an effect or pending effect is resolving, finish resolving that effect or pending effect.

rules.title: When an attack ends, resolve any pending effects that are already pending for the current timing window.
rules.text: 9.28. When an attack ends, resolve any pending effects that are already pending for the current timing window.

rules.title: After an attack ends and all effects and pending effects for the current timing window have resolved, remove effects…
rules.text: 9.29. After an attack ends and all effects and pending effects for the current timing window have resolved, remove effects that last “while attacking,” “while stealing,” “while fighting” and variations thereof. The turn player’s Main Phase continues.

rules.title: An effect is card text that affects the game.
rules.text: 10.1. An effect is card text that affects the game. Card text is the source of effects.

rules.title: Within card text, a line break indicates the end of the effect text.
rules.text: 10.1.1. Within card text, a line break indicates the end of the effect text.

rules.title: Each separate paragraph on a card is considered a single effect.
rules.text: 10.1.2. Each separate paragraph on a card is considered a single effect.

rules.title: When an effect refers to “this card,” “this Unit,” “this Legend,” “this Gear,” or another similar phrase, it refers t…
rules.text: 10.1.3. When an effect refers to “this card,” “this Unit,” “this Legend,” “this Gear,” or another similar phrase, it refers to the source of that effect unless another rule or effect says otherwise.

rules.title: If you control the source of an effect, it is considered “your” effect.
rules.text: 10.1.4. If you control the source of an effect, it is considered “your” effect. You are the one who resolves it.

rules.title: There are four types of effects: triggered effects, activated effects, permanent effects, and replacement effects.
rules.text: 10.4. There are four types of effects: triggered effects, activated effects, permanent effects, and replacement effects.

rules.title: A “triggered effect” becomes pending when its trigger condition is met.
rules.text: 10.4.1. A “triggered effect” becomes pending when its trigger condition is met.

rules.title: You may use an “activated effect” at your discretion during your Main Phase.
rules.text: 10.4.2. You may use an “activated effect” at your discretion during your Main Phase.

rules.title: A “persistent effect” continuously applies while its conditions (if any) are met.
rules.text: 10.4.3. A “persistent effect” continuously applies while its conditions (if any) are met.

rules.title: A “replacement effect” replaces one game action or process with another.
rules.text: 10.4.4. A “replacement effect” replaces one game action or process with another.

rules.title: An effect is “valid” if it can apply according to its text, the game rules, and the current game state.
rules.text: 10.5. An effect is “valid” if it can apply according to its text, the game rules, and the current game state.

rules.title: An effect is “invalid” if it cannot apply according to its text, the game rules, or the current game state.
rules.text: 10.6. An effect is “invalid” if it cannot apply according to its text, the game rules, or the current game state.

rules.title: If all of an effect is invalid, ignore that effect.
rules.text: 10.6.1. If all of an effect is invalid, ignore that effect.

rules.title: If part of an effect is invalid, ignore the invalid part and resolve as much of the remaining effect as possible.
rules.text: 10.6.2. If part of an effect is invalid, ignore the invalid part and resolve as much of the remaining effect as possible.

rules.title: Even if an effect is invalid, it is still considered an effect on the card.
rules.text: 10.6.3. Even if an effect is invalid, it is still considered an effect on the card.

rules.title: A persistent effect continuously applies while it is active.
rules.text: 10.22. A persistent effect continuously applies while it is active.

rules.title: A persistent effect is not activated.
rules.text: 10.22.1. A persistent effect is not activated.

rules.title: A persistent effect never becomes pending.
rules.text: 10.22.2. A persistent effect never becomes pending.

rules.title: A persistent effect applies only while its source is in the area where that effect is active.
rules.text: 10.22.3. A persistent effect applies only while its source is in the area where that effect is active.

rules.title: If a persistent effect has a duration, it applies only for that duration.
rules.text:
10.23. If a persistent effect has a duration, it applies only for that duration.

> **EXAMPLE:** A Unit's effect text reads "Other friendly Units have +2 power while attacking.” The Unit only gains +2 from the moment the Unit attacks until the attack ends.

rules.title: When a persistent effect’s duration ends, that effect stops applying immediately once there are no other pending effe…
rules.text: 10.23.1. When a persistent effect’s duration ends, that effect stops applying immediately once there are no other pending effects.

rules.title: Pay
“Pay” is a game action in which you spend a number of Eddies and/or Legends in the Legends area equal to a cost.
rules.text: 11.8.1. “Pay” is a game action in which you spend a number of Eddies and/or Legends in the Legends area equal to a cost.

rules.title: Effects that reduce the amount you pay to play a card or activate an effect do not change the card’s cost value, nor…
rules.text: 11.8.2. Effects that reduce the amount you pay to play a card or activate an effect do not change the card’s cost value, nor the activation cost value.

rules.title: Effects that reduce the amount you pay to play a card or activate an effect cannot reduce the amount below 1.
rules.text: 11.8.3. Effects that reduce the amount you pay to play a card or activate an effect cannot reduce the amount below 1.

rules.title: When you play a card “for Free,” play the card without paying its cost.
rules.text: 11.8.4. When you play a card “for Free,” play the card without paying its cost.

rules.title: When playing a card for free, you must still meet any additional conditions outside of the cost.
rules.text: 11.8.4.1. When playing a card for free, you must still meet any additional conditions outside of the cost.

rules.title: Call a Legend
rules.text: 11.11. ### Call a Legend

rules.title: “Call a Legend” is a game action in which you pay 1 €$ to flip a face-down Legend face-up.
rules.text: 11.11.1. “Call a Legend” is a game action in which you pay 1 €$ to flip a face-down Legend face-up.

rules.title: You may choose any one (1) friendly face-down Legend in your Legends area.
rules.text: 11.11.1.1. You may choose any one (1) friendly face-down Legend in your Legends area.

rules.title: A Legend flipped face-up through the Call a Legend action is a “called” Legend.
rules.text: 11.11.1.2. A Legend flipped face-up through the Call a Legend action is a “called” Legend.

rules.title: The called Legend maintains its orientation (spent or ready) when flipped face-up.
rules.text: 11.11.1.3. The called Legend maintains its orientation (spent or ready) when flipped face-up.

rules.title: When you flip a Legend face up this way it activates any [CALL] keyword effects on that Legend.
rules.text: 11.11.1.4. When you flip a Legend face up this way it activates any [CALL] keyword effects on that Legend. See [CALL].

rules.title: You may only Call a Legend once per turn.
rules.text: 11.11.2. You may only Call a Legend once per turn.

rules.title: You may Call a Legend as an action during your main phase.
rules.text: 11.11.2.1. You may Call a Legend as an action during your main phase.

rules.title: You may Call a Legend as a reaction when a rival Unit attacks.
rules.text: 11.11.2.2. You may Call a Legend as a reaction when a rival Unit attacks.

rules.title: [BLOCKER]
The [BLOCKER] keyword is shorthand for “When a rival Unit attacks, you may spend this Unit to redirect the attack to…
rules.text: 11.24.1. The [BLOCKER] keyword is shorthand for “When a rival Unit attacks, you may spend this Unit to redirect the attack to it instead.“

rules.title: Activate [BLOCKER] as a reaction during the React Step of your Rival’s attack action.
rules.text: 11.24.2. Activate [BLOCKER] as a reaction during the React Step of your Rival’s attack action.

rules.title: When a Unit uses [BLOCKER], it becomes the target of the attacking Unit’s current attack.
rules.text: 11.24.3. When a Unit uses [BLOCKER], it becomes the target of the attacking Unit’s current attack.

rules.title: [GO SOLO]
The [GO SOLO] keyword is shorthand for “Pay this Legend's cost to play it as a ready Unit.
rules.text: 11.25.1. The [GO SOLO] keyword is shorthand for “Pay this Legend's cost to play it as a ready Unit. It can attack this turn. If it leaves the field, remove it from the game.”

decisions.continuous: 10.4.3,10.22–10.23: persistent, never activated/pending; derive live source/target contribution.
decisions.source: Face-up Legend in LEGENDS (3.4.1,4.3–4.5,5.7,10.22.3). Spent is orientation, not loss of effect; no readiness condition. Null cost prohibits current field play; no future move mechanic inferred.
decisions.attacking: 9.3–9.5: after locked target/spend/declaration, across pending effects/React/Fight/Steal through9.29 cleanup. Target selection is not attacking. Persistent duration ends after pending effects (10.23.1).
decisions.power: Add before existing comparison/reference clamps and query current power at actual Fight/Steal; FAQ confirms both.
